items.name: Destructive Power
entries: When you roll damage for a power, you can gain strain equal to half the power's order (minimum 1 strain) to make half the damage dice you rolled deal the die's maximum value instead of the number rolled.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Dynamic Power
entries: When a Medium or smaller creature is hit by an attack roll for a power you manifest or fails a saving throw against a power you manifest, you can gain 2 strain to move the target up to 15 feet in any direction or knock them {@condition prone}. You can gain 3 strain to affect a Large creature with this Psionic Exertion option, or 4 strain to affect a Huge creature.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Expanded Power
entries: After you make a manifestation test to {@action Manifest a Power|TalPsi|manifest a power} that creates an area of effect, you can gain strain equal to the power's order to double all dimensions of the area of effect.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Fascinating Power
entries: When a creature fails a saving throw against a power you manifest, you can activate this Psionic Exertion option. If the creature has a challenge rating equal to or lower than your talent level (or if its level is equal to or lower than your talent level, for creatures that don't have a challenge rating), you gain 2 strain and the target is {@condition charmed} by you for 1 minute or until you or your companions do anything harmful to it. If the creature has a challenge rating or level higher than your talent level, you gain no strain and the target is unaffected.
A creature {@condition charmed} in this way is friendly to you. When the condition ends for the target, they know they were {@condition charmed} by you.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Halting Power
entries: When a Medium or smaller creature fails a saving throw against a power you manifest, you can gain 2 strain to make the target {@condition restrained} until the start of your next turn. You can gain 4 strain to affect a Large creature with this Psionic Exertion option.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Magnified Power
entries: After you make a manifestation test to {@action Manifest a Power|TalPsi|manifest a power} that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can gain 1 strain to double its duration, to a maximum of 24 hours.

Alternatively, after you make a manifestation test to {@action Manifest a Power|TalPsi|manifest a power} that has a range of 5 feet or greater, you can gain 1 strain to double the range of the power. After you make a manifestation test to {@action Manifest a Power|TalPsi|manifest a power} that has a range of touch, you can gain 1 strain to make the range of the power 30 feet.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Overwhelming Power
entries: When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against a power you manifest, you can gain strain equal to the power's order to force the creature to reroll the saving throw with a penalty equal to your proficiency bonus. The creature must use the new roll.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Shared Power
entries: After you make a manifestation test to {@action Manifest a Power|TalPsi|manifest a power} that can target only one creature and doesn't create an area of effect, you can gain strain equal to the power's order to target a second creature in range with the same power.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Terrifying Power
entries: When a creature fails a saving throw against a power you manifest, you can activate this Psionic Exertion option. If the creature has a challenge rating equal to or lower than your talent level (or if its level is equal to or lower than your talent level, for creatures that don't have a challenge rating), you gain 3 strain and the target is {@condition frightened} of you for 1 minute. If the creature has a challenge rating or level higher than your talent level, you gain no strain and the target is unaffected.
Whenever a creature frightened in this way takes damage, they make a Wisdom saving throw against your talent power save DC, ending the condition on themself on a success.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Acquired Tolerance
entries: You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you gain resistance to poison damage. In addition, you automatically succeed on saving throws against your own apothecary spells, and never take damage from your own apothecary spells.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Adrenaline Surge
entries: A creature at 0 hit points who regains hit points from a spell you cast using an apothecary spell slot gains resistance to all damage and has advantage on saving throws until the end of its next turn. It gains advantage on the first attack roll it makes on its next turn.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Anatomical Precision
entries: When you make a weapon attack, you can use your Intelligence modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity, for the attack and damage rolls.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Anesthesiology
entries: You can cast {@spell hold person} without expending a spell slot or requiring material components. You must finish a long rest before you can use this theory on the same creature again.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Bedside Manner
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Insight} and {@skill Persuasion} skills. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of these skills.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Caustic Formulae
entries: Once per turn when you deal damage to a creature or object with an apothecary spell, you can expend an apothecary spell slot to deal {@dice 2d4} extra acid damage to that target, plus another {@dice 2d4} per level of the spell slot.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Clinical Conditioning
entries: You gain proficiency in Constitution saving throws.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Combat Medic
entries: You gain proficiency with martial weapons and shields.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Corrosive Compound
entries: When you deal poison damage with your apothecary spells, you can choose to deal half the spell's damage as poison damage and half the spell's damage as acid damage instead.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Cosmetic Surgery
entries: You can spend 8 hours performing an occult surgical procedure upon a willing creature, permanently transforming its appearance. You decide what the creature looks like, including facial features, the sound of its voice, hair length, coloration, and distinguishing characteristics, but none of its game statistics change. You can't alter the size of a creature, and its basic shape stays the same. The resulting transformation is non-magical, however, a {@spell greater restoration} spell or similar magic cast upon the creature can restore it to its original appearance.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Critical Condition
entries: When a creature rolls a natural 1 on a saving throw made against one of your {@filter apothecary spells that deals damage|spells|source=|class=apothecary (scgtd)|damage type=acid;bludgeoning;cold;fire;force;lightning;necrotic;piercing;poison;psychic;radiant;slashing;thunder|saving throw=strength;dexterity;constitution;intelligence;wisdom;charisma}, roll all of the spell's damage dice twice and add them together. Then add any relevant modifiers as normal to determine the damage that creature takes from the spell.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Diagnosis
entries: You can take the {@action Help} action as a bonus action on your turn.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Doctor's Note
entries: You can cast the {@spell sending} spell at-will. You must finish a long rest before you can use this theory to contact the same creature again.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Double Dose
entries: When you cast an apothecary spell using an {@filter apothecary spell slot that targets a single creature and restores hit points|spells|source=|class=apothecary (scgtd)|components & miscellaneous=hl;!reprinted|area style=st} to that creature, you can target an additional creature within range.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Extracurricular Research
entries: You learn two additional cantrips of your choice from any class's spell list. These cantrips become apothecary cantrips for you.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Inoculation
entries: You have resistance to necrotic damage, and your hit point maximum can't be reduced. In addition, you are immune to diseases.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Interdisciplinary Practice
entries: When you use your action to cast a spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Laboratory Assistant
entries: You learn the spell {@spell find familiar}, and always have this spell prepared. It doesn't count against the number of apothecary spells you can prepare.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Liability Insurance
entries: You can cast {@spell contingency} once on yourself without material components. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Medical Expertise
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Medicine} and {@skill Nature} skills. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of these skills.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Medical Lexicon
entries: You learn six languages of your choice. You can cast {@spell detect poison and disease} at will.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Nerve Agent
entries: When you deal poison damage with your apothecary spells, you can choose to deal psychic damage instead.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Noxious Blood
entries: When a creature hits you with a melee attack while within 5 feet of you, it takes poison damage equal to {@dice 1d6} + your Constitution modifier.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Pharmacology
entries: When you cast a spell using an apothecary spell slot or your Greater Formula feature which restores hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to your Intelligence modifier.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Physiological Analysis
entries: If you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its physiology. The Game Master reveals to you two of the following characteristics of your choice:
Alternatively, you can spend 1 minute observing a corpse. After 1 minute, you determine the cause of death.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Practical Resuscitation
entries: When you cast a spell that has the sole effect of restoring a creature to life (but not undeath), such as {@spell raise dead}, you don't need material components to cast the spell if the creature has died within the past hour.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Putrefaction
entries: Your apothecary spells and abilities ignore undead creatures' resistance or immunity to poison damage and immunity to the {@condition poisoned} condition.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Rapid Response
entries: When you cast an apothecary spell that restores hit points to a creature, before or after casting the spell, you can move your speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Routine Procedure
entries: You can cast {@spell lesser restoration} at-will without expending a spell slot.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Stolen Secrets
entries: You learn one spell from any class's spell list. It must be of a level for which you have apothecary spell slots or lower. The spell is treated as an apothecary spell for you, and doesn't count against the number of apothecary spells you know.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Subject Preparation
entries: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, that creature has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes against an apothecary spell you cast before the end of your next turn.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Surgeon's Instinct
entries: You have {@sense blindsight} out to a range of 10 feet.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Surgical Strikes
entries: You can attack twice, instead of once, when you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Toxicology
entries: You add your Intelligence modifier to the damage rolls of spells that deal poison damage.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Triage
entries: You learn the {@spell spare the dying} cantrip if you don't know it already. When you cast this cantrip, it has a range of 60 feet.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Unfailing Focus
entries: When you fail a Constitution saving throw to maintain {@status concentration} on an apothecary spell, you can choose to succeed instead. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Venomous Instruments
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, the creature takes extra poison damage equal to your Intelligence modifier.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Virulence
entries: When you roll a 1 on a damage die for an apothecary spell that deals poison damage, you can reroll the die. You must use the new result, even if the new roll is a 1.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Vital Signs
entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw or death saving throw, you can use your reaction to add your Intelligence modifier to the creature's roll, potentially turning a failure into a success. You must finish a short rest before you can use this theory on the same creature again.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory

items.name: Vivisection
entries: Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a 19 or 20.
items.subtitle: Esoteric Theory
